<summary>Agent "Research turbo model swap candidates" completed</summary>
<result># Local Model Stack Research — Turbo Candidates for the TDD Pipeline

Research date: 2026-06-10. Headline finding up front: **the Qwen world moved under you.** Since your stack was set, Qwen shipped the 2507 refreshes (July 2025), Qwen3.5 (Feb–Mar 2026), and Qwen3.6 (April 2026). The best reasoning-per-GB checkpoint today is not a Qwen3-30B-A3B variant at all — it's **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit-DWQ at 20.7GB**, which beats your current 30GB 8bit on quality while being ~10GB smaller and roughly 2x faster to decode.

---

## 1. Qwen3-30B-A3B variants (mlx-community)

**Sizes on disk:**

| Checkpoint | Disk | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-8bit (current) | ~30–32.5GB | your baseline |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-6bit | ~24.8GB | quality ≈ bf16 within noise |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-4bit-DWQ | **17.2GB** | DWQ distilled 6bit→4bit |
| Instruct-2507 / Thinking-2507 quants | same arch, same sizes per bit-width | |

**Quality:**
- An [mlx-lm discussion (#616)](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/discussions/616) found 6bit matching or even exceeding bf16 on task accuracy (maintainer attributes the "exceeding" to sampling variance, but the takeaway stands: **6bit ≈ full precision, 8bit buys you nothing measurable**). Your 8bit checkpoint is paying ~6–8GB of rent for statistical noise.
- The [4bit-DWQ](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen3-30B-A3B-4bit-DWQ) is a learned quant distilled from the 6bit — recovers most of the 4bit quality loss at 17.2GB.
- **2507 refreshes are a straight upgrade over the original hybrid model**: [Thinking-2507](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507) scores AIME'25 80.5 (the original 30B-A3B scored ~70.9; the [Instruct-2507](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507) scores 61.3 without thinking). Significant gains in reasoning, coding, tool use, and 256K native context ([SiliconFlow](https://www.siliconflow.com/models/qwen3-30b-a3b-thinking-2507), [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/models/qwen/qwen3-30b-a3b-thinking-2507)).

**Best single reasoning checkpoint under ~32GB within this family:** `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507` at 6bit (~24.8GB) for max quality, or 4bit-DWQ (~17.2GB) for max speed. But see the Qwen3.6 finding below — it obsoletes this question.

**The leapfrog option:** [mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit-DWQ](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit-DWQ) — **20.7GB on disk**, 35B total / 3B active MoE, released 2026-04-16, multimodal, 262K context, Apache 2.0. Per [llmbase.ai](https://llmbase.ai/compare/qwen3-30b-a3b-2507,qwen3-6-35b-a3b/) and [InsiderLLM](https://insiderllm.com/guides/qwen35-local-guide-which-model-fits-your-gpu/): GPQA 84.1, **SWE-bench Verified 73.4** (up from 69.2 on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B), Terminal-Bench 51.5, plus "thinking preservation" across turns ([QwenLM/Qwen3.6 GitHub](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3.6)). That is a different class of model than 30B-A3B-2507 at two-thirds the disk size of your current 8bit.

## 2. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B

- Arch: 30.5B total / 3.3B active, 128 experts (8 active), 262K native context, instruct-only (no thinking mode) ([HF card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct)).
- Sizes: 4bit ≈ 17.5GB, 6bit ≈ 24.8GB, 8bit ≈ 32.5GB ([lmstudio-community MLX-4bit](https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-MLX-4bit)); a [4bit-DWQ](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit-DWQ) and dwq-v2 exist on mlx-community.
- **SWE-bench Verified ~51.6%** with OpenHands/100 turns ([HF discussion](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct/discussions/30)) — trained with long-horizon agentic RL, strong tool calling ([DigitalOcean writeup](https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/qwen3-coder-agentic-coding-model)).
- **Would it beat stock 30B-A3B for act/implement?** Yes, clearly — it's purpose-built for multi-turn edit/test loops. **But it loses to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (51.6 vs 73.4 SWE-bench) at the same disk size.** The dedicated coder model is no longer justified unless you want a frozen, battle-tested tool-call format.

## 3. Tiny extraction model (<6GB)

| Candidate | Disk (4bit MLX) | Why / Why not |
|---|---|---|
| **Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit** | **~5.6GB** | Released 2026-03-02; matches/beats GPT-OSS-120B on several benchmarks; function calling + 262K context; IFBench 76.5 family score for instruction following ([mlx-community card](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit), [llm-stats](https://llm-stats.com/models/qwen3.5-9b)) |
| **LFM2.5-8B-A1B** (4bit ≈ 4.7GB; 8bit = 9GB) | ~4.7GB | MoE with only **1.5B active** — fastest in class, 253 t/s on M5 Max, day-one MLX support, native function calling ([Liquid AI blog](https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-8b-a1b), [MLX-8bit card](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-8B-A1B-MLX-8bit)) |
| Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-4bit | ~2.3GB | Same arch as everything you already run; zero-risk; weaker than the two above |
| Phi-4-mini (3.8B) | ~2.5GB | Strong reasoning-per-param but weaker tool-call ecosystem on MLX ([promptquorum](https://www.promptquorum.com/power-local-llm/mobile-llm-models-phi4-gemma-smollm)) |

Caveat: small-model structured output degrades at 4bit; tools like [Rapid-MLX](https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX) exist specifically to repair broken 4bit tool-calls. For a decide-model whose only job is schema-filling, prefer 6–8bit on the tiny model — you have the headroom.

## 4. MoE-specific MLX speedups (2025–2026)

- MLX went "experimental to fastest option" on Apple Silicon in this window; **MoE models see up to 3x vs Ollama and ~1.46x vs raw llama.cpp/Metal** ([yage.ai MLX deep-dive, 2026-03](https://yage.ai/share/mlx-apple-silicon-en-20260331.html)). Roughly half the Ollama gap is Ollama's Go wrapper overhead.
- MLX MoE memory is leaner too: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B = 34.7GB resident on MLX vs 40GB GGUF (~13% saving).
- MLX's known weak spot is **prefill/TTFT on long prompts** (it spent 94% of time on prefill in one 650-token test). Mitigation: **oMLX's persistent KV cache compresses repeated-prefix TTFT from 30–90s to 1–3s** — directly relevant to your ReAct loop where the system prompt + transcript prefix repeats every turn, and you already have oMLX queued as the Epic-24 backend.
- Recommended settings: keep peak below ~75% of unified memory (48GB on your 64GB box — your existing ceiling is exactly right); raise the GPU wired limit (`sudo sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb=...`) rather than letting macOS page — that paging spiral is what produced your kernel reboot; keep `kv_bits=8` (you already do); quantized KV is the main A3B-class lever besides bit-width. One quality caveat: MoE routers are **more sensitive to aggressive quantization** than dense models (mis-routed experts), which is why DWQ/6bit checkpoints matter more for A3B than for dense 30Bs ([sitepoint MLX guide](https://www.sitepoint.com/llama-4-scout-on-mlx-the-complete-apple-silicon-guide-2026/)).

## 5. Real-world M-series t/s (Mac mini M2/M4 Pro class)

- **Mac mini M4 Pro 64GB, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (4bit MLX): ~130 t/s decode** ([yage.ai measured](https://yage.ai/share/mlx-apple-silicon-en-20260331.html)); a more conservative report says 32 t/s on M4 Pro for an 8bit/GGUF config ([willitrunai](https://willitrunai.com/macs/m4-pro-64gb)) — the spread is quant + runtime, not hardware. Expect **80–130 t/s at 4bit, ~45–60 t/s at 8bit** on M4 Pro; M2 Pro (200GB/s) lands at roughly 60–70% of that. M2 Max pulls 68 t/s, M4 Max 100+ at 4bit ([arsturn guide](https://www.arsturn.com/blog/running-qwen3-coder-30b-at-full-context-memory-requirements-performance-tips), [HN thread](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=43856489)).
- Qwen3.5/3.6-35B-A3B behaves identically (same 3B active): ~130 t/s on M4-class MLX ([llmcheck.net](https://llmcheck.net/benchmarks), [willitrunai Qwen3.5 guide](https://willitrunai.com/blog/qwen-3-5-mlx-apple-silicon-guide)).
- The A3B decode rule of thumb: ~3B active params × bytes/param ÷ memory bandwidth. **Halving bit-width from your 8bit roughly doubles decode t/s** — this is the single biggest "turbo" lever available to you.

---

# Recommended Stack

## Primary ("turbo") — 26.3GB total resident

| Role | Checkpoint | Disk | Expected t/s (M4 Pro / M2 Pro class) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Think + Code (one model) | `mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit-DWQ` | 20.7GB | ~100–130 / ~60–80 |
| Decide / extract | `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit` (or 6bit, ~8GB, still fits) | 5.6GB | ~60–90 / ~40–60 |

**~26GB resident vs your current ~35GB** — both models stay loaded simultaneously with ~22GB headroom for KV cache and the OS. No model swap latency between think and decide phases. Quality goes *up* (SWE-bench 73.4-class vs 2505-era 30B-A3B), decode speed roughly doubles, and the dedicated coder model becomes unnecessary — Qwen3.6-35B-A3B beats Coder-30B-A3B by 20+ points on SWE-bench at the same size.

**Migration risk: MODERATE.**
- New architecture tag (`qwen3_5_moe`, Gated DeltaNet hybrid on the 9B) — **requires a recent mlx-lm; verify your pinned version and oMLX support before deleting anything.**
- Qwen3.6's "thinking preservation" changes the chat template / think-block handling — your transcript parsing and extraction prompts need a test pass.
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is multimodal; confirm the text-only path in mlx-lm is clean.
- DWQ at 4bit on a MoE: run your gate suite against the 8bit baseline before cutover; if quality regresses, `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-6bit` (~27GB) still fits.

## Conservative ("same family, just better") — 36.7GB total

| Role | Checkpoint | Disk | Expected t/s (M4 Pro) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Think | `mlx-community/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507` 4bit-DWQ | ~17.2GB | ~100–130 |

# Turbo Quantization Research — Model Stack Upgrades

**RUN_ID:** 20260610-210005 · **Date:** 2026-06-10
**Sources:** two parallel research agents — (1) MLX quantization techniques (DWQ/AWQ/QAT/KV/spec-decode), (2) model swap candidates. Full agent reports archived in session transcript.

## TL;DR

Current stack (Qwen3-30B-A3B-**8bit** think + gemma-4-e4b-it-**4bit** decide, ~35GB resident) is paying ~13GB of memory rent for quality that measurements say doesn't exist. Both agents converge independently on the same conclusion: **4-bit DWQ is the lever**. A3B MoE models are unusually quantization-robust — a 4-bit DWQ of Qwen3-30B-A3B *outperformed the plain 6-bit quant* in published evals, and 6-bit ≈ bf16 within noise (mlx-lm #616).

Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound on Apple Silicon, so halving weight bits ≈ doubling tokens/sec. The 8-bit think model buys nothing measurable.

## Tiered recommendations

### Tier 0 — free, do now (zero migration risk)

| Swap | From | To | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decide model | `gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit` | [`mlx-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-4bit`](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-4bit) | Same ~4.9GB, same speed, QAT (Google fine-tuned for int4) ≈ bf16-like quality vs post-hoc quant. Drop-in. |

### Tier 1 — conservative turbo (LOW risk, same architecture, ~2x decode)

| Role | Checkpoint | Disk |
|---|---|---|
| Think | `mlx-community/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507` 4bit-DWQ | ~17.2GB |
| (optional) Code/act | `mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit-dwq-v2` | ~17.2GB |
| Decide | gemma-4-E4B QAT (Tier 0) or `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-4bit` | 4.9 / 2.3GB |

- 2507 refresh is a straight upgrade over the original 30B-A3B (AIME'25 80.5 vs ~70.9; better tool use, 256K native ctx).
- 8bit→4bit DWQ: 30GB → 17.2GB (−13GB), est. ~35 t/s → ~55–60 t/s on this hardware.
- Quality ≈ the plain 6-bit (i.e. ≈ bf16); A3B MoE punches above the quant curve.
- Integration notes: Thinking-2507 is always-thinking (no `/no_think`); Coder uses Qwen's XML-ish tool-call format (we don't depend on native tool-call parsing — ReAct loop extracts from text — so low impact).

### Tier 2 — leapfrog (MODERATE risk, generation upgrade)

| Role | Checkpoint | Disk |
|---|---|---|
| Think + code (one model) | [`mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit-DWQ`](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit-DWQ) | 20.7GB |
| Decide | [`mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit`](https://huggingface.co/mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit) (prefer 6bit ~8GB for schema-fill reliability) | 5.6–8GB |

- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: **SWE-bench Verified 73.4** (vs ~51.6 for Coder-30B-A3B), GPQA 84.1, 262K ctx, Apache 2.0, same 3B-active decode speed class (~60–80 t/s here).
- ~26–29GB resident total vs current ~35GB; both models co-resident with KV headroom; well under the 48GB ceiling.
- Unlocks **DFlash block-diffusion drafting** in oMLX (experimental): 2–4x further decode on greedy code-gen, single-request, ≤4K ctx path. Draft checkpoints exist only for Qwen3.5/3.6 + Gemma 4 — our current Qwen3-30B-A3B can never use it.
- **Verify before cutover:** mlx-lm pinned version + oMLX support the `qwen3_5_moe` arch tags; Qwen3.6 "thinking preservation" changes the chat template → re-test `_THINK_TAG_RE` stripping and extraction prompts; run the gate suite against the 8bit baseline; confirm clean text-only path (model is multimodal).

### Anti-recommendations (measured, not vibes)

- **Never enable classic `--draft-model` speculative decoding on A3B targets.** 25–45% *slowdowns* measured on MoE with small active params (mlx-lm #1132); 19/19 configs lost to baseline on llama.cpp; history of token-skip bugs with Qwen3 spec decode (mlx-lm #846). Rule of thumb: speculation loses when target *active* params are within ~4x of draft total size — A3B has 3B active.
- **Q2 / mixed_2_6 quants** — catastrophic (Llama-8B Q2 ppl ≈ 2,132). Useful floor is ~4 bpw uniform or ~5 bpw mixed.
- **kv_bits < 8** — 4-bit K-cache destroys greedy decode on MLX. Hold kv_bits=8 (current setting is correct).

### Watch list

- **TurboQuant/PolarQuant KV compression** — 4.6x KV compression at 98% decode speed via fused Metal kernels; not yet in mlx-lm mainline (track [mlx-lm #1060](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/issues/1060)). Matters when long-context agent sessions make KV, not weights, the bottleneck.
- **MTPLX / oMLX MTP integration** ([omlx #1089](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/issues/1089)) — Qwen3.6's native MTP heads as self-drafter, 2.24x decode measured. Another reason the Tier 2 generation upgrade compounds.
- **Custom ~5 bpw mixed DWQ** (`mlx_lm.dwq --target-bpw 5.0`) — fallback if 4bit-DWQ regresses on our evals; DDWQ at 5 bpw beats uniform 5-bit in both ppl and t/s (power-of-2 kernels).
- **LFM2.5-8B-A1B** (1.5B active, ~4.7GB at 4bit, 253 t/s class) — alternative decide model if gemma QAT underperforms.

## System settings (either tier)

- Keep the **48GB total-weights ceiling** (pipe-model-tiers rule) — the Qwen3-Coder-Next-4bit kernel-reboot was macOS paging, not MLX. Consider raising `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` via sysctl rather than letting macOS page.
- oMLX prefix/SSD cache already configured (50GB at /Volumes/Extra/omlx-cache) — directly attacks MLX's known prefill/TTFT weakness for our repeating ReAct prefix (30–90s → 1–3s on repeated prefixes).

## Suggested order of operations

1. Pull gemma-4-E4B QAT, swap config, run M1 driver — should be invisible-or-better. (Tier 0)
2. Pull Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 4bit-DWQ (17.2GB), swap think tier, re-run M1 + the 87-test suite + a live fixture run; compare step counts/escalations vs the 8bit baseline runs. (Tier 1)
3. If Tier 1 holds quality: delete the 30GB 8bit checkpoint, reclaim disk.
4. Separately evaluate Tier 2 (Qwen3.6) once mlx-lm/oMLX arch support is confirmed — it's the path to DFlash/MTP turbo decode, which Tier 1 models can never use.

## Context

M1 of datum-local is proven and hardened: the ReAct agent loop (THINK→DECIDE→ASSEMBLE→EXECUTE→OBSERVE) survived 5 live runs and an adversarial review (8 findings — 6 fixed inline with regression tests, 2 filed as #60/#61; 87/87 tests green). The user has now given explicit approval to merge to main and start the next phase: the **Tier 0+1 model swap** from the turbo-quantization research (`datum-local/docs/turbo-quant-research-20260610-210005.md`) — ~2x decode speed, −13GB memory, quality ≈ current 8bit, low migration risk (same architecture family).

Current state:
- **datum** (`gitrdunhq/datum`): `feat/react-agent-loop` is 2 commits ahead of `main` (8e72d6d feat + 6d2b3e2 fix), clean tree, branch never pushed. Repo merges PRs squash-style (#59, #56).
- **datum-local**: separate local-only repo (no remote), already on trunk `master`; only the turbo research doc is uncommitted.

## Part A — Merge datum to main (PR workflow)

1. `git fetch origin` and verify local `main` == `origin/main` (tip b84f343).
2. **Squash before first push** (two-phase rule; branch is unpublished): on `feat/react-agent-loop`, `git reset --soft main` then one commit:
   `feat(agent-loop): ReAct loop for local-model tool calling` — body covers the loop architecture, tier-1 guards, context monitor, rules-registry integration, adversarial-review hardening. **No AI attribution.**
3. Push: `git push -u origin feat/react-agent-loop`.
4. `unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh pr create` — title matches the commit; body summarizes M1 results + review outcome, references #60/#61 as follow-ups. No AI attribution.
5. `unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`, then `git checkout main && git pull`.
6. Update memory `project-datum-local-variant.md`: merged, PR number, M1 thread closed.

## Part B — datum-local housekeeping

1. On `datum-local` master: commit the research doc — `docs: turbo quantization research (RUN_ID 20260610-210005)`.

## Part C — Tier 0+1 model swap

### Downloads (HF_HUB_CACHE=/Volumes/Extra/mlx-models, set before any HF call)

| Tier | Checkpoint | Size | Replaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `mlx-community/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-4bit` | ~4.9GB | gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit (DECIDE) |
| 1 | `mlx-community/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-4bit-DWQ` | ~17.2GB | Qwen3-30B-A3B-8bit (THINK) |

Verify exact repo names on HF before download (research cited the family; exact Thinking-2507 DWQ slug needs confirmation). Fallbacks in order: `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-4bit-DWQ`, then `Qwen3-30B-A3B-4bit-DWQ-053125`.

### Config changes

- `datum-local/fixtures/toy-project/.datum/config.toml` + datum root `config.toml`: `model` → new DWQ checkpoint, `fast_model` → gemma QAT name. Keep `context_window = 131072`, `kv_bits = 8`, `timeout_s = 600`.
- **YaRN patch no longer needed**: 2507 models are 256K-native (the old 8bit snapshot's `config.json` rope_scaling hack stays with the old model; new model untouched). oMLX `max_context_window 131072` stays.
- oMLX: confirm both new models load and report sane context via the admin endpoint before driver runs.

### Validation (compare against run-5 baseline: RED 3 steps/75s, GREEN 5/103s, REFACTOR 5/65s)

1. `uv run pytest` — full 87-test suite (model-independent, should stay green).
2. Reset the toy-project fixture, run `m1_driver.py` live end-to-end (RED→GREEN→REFACTOR with pytest gates).
3. Record steps/tokens/wall-clock per phase + decode t/s from oMLX usage; expect ~1.5–2x decode improvement, equal-or-better step counts.
4. Watch for Thinking-2507 quirks: always-thinking (no `/no_think`) — `_THINK_TAG_RE` in `datum/agent_loop.py` already strips closed and unclosed `<think>` blocks, so this should be absorbed; confirm fenced-content extraction still finds the code block after longer reasoning.
5. If quality regresses (more steps, escalations, or guard trips than baseline): revert config to 8bit, keep DWQ on disk, note findings.

### Cleanup (only after validation passes)

- Old 8bit checkpoint (30GB) deletion is destructive — surface to user, don't auto-delete.
- Update memory `project-model-stack.md` with the new stack + measured numbers.

## Verification (end-to-end)

- `gh pr view` shows merged PR; `git log main -1` on datum shows the squashed commit.
- datum-local `git log` shows the docs commit.
- M1 driver completes headlessly on the new stack; fixture git history shows feat + refactor commits; phase timings logged and compared to baseline.
- 87/87 tests green.

## Out of scope (explicitly)

- Tier 2 leapfrog (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash) — needs mlx-lm/oMLX arch-support verification first; documented in the research doc.
- M2 orchestrator — next after this lands.
- datum-local remote/push — repo stays local-only.

Approved 2026-06-10 (architecture only, no implementation yet). Full plan: `~/.claude/plans/i-would-like-to-cozy-eclipse.md`.

**Decisions (user-confirmed):**
- `gitrdunhq/datum-local/` sibling repo (like turret split), datum as **editable path dependency** (`../datum`) — datum's wheel packaging is broken (assets/references/lane-tools not packaged; path_utils resolves from source tree), so non-editable installs don't work until fixed (M7).
- **Strictly local, no Claude escalation** — LocalEscalationPolicy: retry w/ jitter → self-consistency vote → local tier escalation (fast→main→new `big` tier) → scope reduction → halt with FailureReport in `.datum/failures/`.
- **Full pipeline headless**: TICKET in → branch + PR out, driven by PipelineDriver + PhaseRunner registry replacing SKILL.md/harness. Distilled prompts (not raw references/*.md) for the 30B model.
- **Chat frontend API-first**: datumd (FastAPI) with state/control/chat endpoints + WebSocket tailing events.jsonl; ChatAgent intent router (command / status Q&A / free chat); web UI + TUI v2 on top. Control hooks designed into PipelineDriver at M2.

**Architecture that made it work — `datum/agent_loop.py` (ReAct), NOT multi_turn_phase:**
- multi_turn_phase's tool path was dead code: prompt never told the model about `action: "tool_execution"`. ReAct loop replaces it for agentic phases; multi_turn stays for analysis phases.

- lane_tools_runner.py manifest was cwd-relative — fixed to resolve via skill_root(); agent loops chdir into the target repo.
- gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit (4.9G) downloaded to /Volumes/Extra/mlx-models, replaces Llama-8B as fast tier. Qwen3-Coder-Next-4bit (42G) is the model that watchdog-rebooted the machine (45G into 64G RAM) — benched.

**Prior-art validation (aider benchmarks):** our design = aider's architect/editor split + `whole` edit format, which beat `diff` for Qwen3-32B (45.8% vs 41.3%, 100% well-formed). Adopt next: ast.parse lint-gate on writes (+3pts in SWE-agent), repair cap of 2 then whole-file re-read, Qwen3 sampling top_p 0.8/top_k 20/temp 0.7.

# datum-local overlay config — local MLX inference with write-tool access
# Copy to .datum/config.toml in the datum-local repo (materialize.sh does this).
#
# This file intentionally configures local-only inference.
# No remote or cloud model IDs appear in this file.

# ── Local LLM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[local_llm]
enabled       = true

# Quality model (30B MoE) for reasoning-intensive phases
model         = "mlx-community/Qwen3-30B-A3B-8bit"

# Fast model (Gemma 4 e4b) for triage, validation, and ReAct DECIDE steps
fast_model    = "mlx-community/gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit"

# Phases handled by the fast model
fast_phases   = ["triage", "validate"]

# All phases routed through local inference
phases        = [
  "triage",
  "act_skeleton",
  "act_red",
  "act_green",
  "act_refactor",
  "validate",
  "sidecar_docs",
  "sidecar_security",
  "closeout_collectors",
]

# Local model cache directory
hf_cache_dir  = "/Volumes/Extra/mlx-models"

# oMLX persistent inference server endpoint
# Start with: brew services start jundot/omlx/omlx
omlx_url      = "http://localhost:12200"

# Generation parameters
max_tokens    = 8192
# 128K via YaRN (factor 4) enabled in the model snapshot's config.json —
# 64 GB RAM holds 30 GB weights + ~6 GB KV at 8-bit with headroom.
# Backup of the pre-YaRN config: config.json.orig in the snapshot dir.
context_window = 131072
temperature   = 0.3

# KV-cache quantization (8-bit saves ~50% memory vs fp16)
kv_bits       = 8
kv_group_size = 64
max_kv_size   = 32768

# ── Multi-Turn Orchestration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Enables multi-step reasoning loops so the local model can plan, read files,
# run tools, and synthesize — all without escalating to a remote model.
[multi_turn]
enabled               = true

# Hard budget caps (all three required when tool execution is on)
max_turns             = 5         # max reasoning turns before forced escalation
timeout_s             = 600       # total wall-clock budget (seconds)
max_tool_turns        = 10        # tool-execution turns before forced escalation

# Tool execution — allows model to call lane tools
enable_tool_execution = true

# Write tools enabled: model may create / modify files inside the sandbox
enable_write_tools    = true

# Allowed tools: 7 read-only lane tools + 3 write tools = 10 total
allowed_tools = [
  # Read-only tools
  "find_callers",
  "filter_gitnexus_output",
  "read_file",
  "read_file_range",
  "list_dir",
  "grep_search",
  "run_command",
  # Write tools (gated by enable_write_tools = true)
  "write_to_file",
  "replace_file_content",
  "multi_replace_file_content",
]

# Write sandbox: only allow writes relative to the project root (cwd)
allowed_write_dirs    = []

# Planning / voting defaults (applied to phases listed above)
turn_timeout_s        = 90    # wall-clock budget for a single turn (seconds)
confidence_threshold  = 0.8   # exit early if model agreement >= this (0.0–1.0)
temperature_schedule  = "fixed"  # "fixed" | "rising" | "falling" | "u_curve"
temperature_min       = 0.2   # floor for scheduled temperature
temperature_max       = 0.7   # ceiling for scheduled temperature
context_reserve_pct   = 20    # % of context window kept free for synthesis output
planning_turn         = true  # turn 0 produces a StepPlan before acting
verification_turn     = true  # final turn synthesises steps into phase schema
two_pass              = true  # freeform draft → grammar extraction (DCCD)
consistency_samples   = 1     # majority-vote samples per turn (1 = fastest)
few_shot              = true  # inject example JSON to anchor output format
phases                = [
  "act_green",
  "act_refactor",
]

# ── Output quality gates ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Thresholds that reject degenerate completions (character floods, repetition).
# Failures here cause a retry on the same turn rather than a hard abort.
[multi_turn.quality_gates]
char_flood_pct  = 0.3   # reject if any single character > 30% of the tail
ngram_size      = 3     # n-gram window for repetition detection
max_count       = 4     # max allowed consecutive identical n-grams
diversity_ratio = 0.25  # min unique-token ratio required in the tail

# ── Per-phase overrides ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# These sections tighten or relax the global [multi_turn] defaults for a
# specific phase. Only the keys listed here are overridden; all others
# inherit from [multi_turn].

# triage: fast, low-confidence classification — fewer turns, rising temperature
[multi_turn.phase_overrides.triage]
max_turns            = 3     # triage rarely needs more than 3 passes
temperature_schedule = "rising"  # encourage broader exploration on retries
confidence_threshold = 0.7   # lower bar — triage is a coarse routing decision

kv_bits       = 8
kv_group_size = 64
max_kv_size   = 32768

# Enables multi-step reasoning loops so the local model can plan, read files,

enabled               = true

# Hard budget caps (all three required when tool execution is on)
max_turns             = 5         # max reasoning turns before forced escalation
timeout_s             = 600       # total wall-clock budget (seconds)
max_tool_turns        = 10        # tool-execution turns before forced escalation

  "run_command",

  "replace_file_content",

]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""M1 driver: bare RED-GREEN cycle via multi_turn_phase with tool execution.

Proves a local model can drive a write-test-commit loop headlessly on the
fixture repo with zero remote/cloud API calls.

Usage:
    python scripts/m1_driver.py --fixture-dir fixtures/toy-project --config .datum/config.toml

Exit codes:
    0  RED-GREEN succeeded, commit created
    1  Structured failure (see .datum/m1-failure.json)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Failure record
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def write_failure_record(
    datum_dir: Path,
    phase: str,
    attempts: int,
    reason: str,
    model: str,
) -> Path:
    """Write a structured JSON failure record and return its path."""
    datum_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    record_path = datum_dir / "m1-failure.json"
    record = {
        "phase": phase,
        "attempts": attempts,
        "reason": reason,
        "model": model,
        "timestamp": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
    }
    record_path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + "\n")
    return record_path


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pytest runner
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def run_pytest(fixture_dir: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    """Run pytest in the fixture directory and return the CompletedProcess."""
    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "--tb=short", "--no-header"],
        cwd=str(fixture_dir),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=120,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Prompts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

RED_PROMPT = """\
Add a FAILING test for a multiply function to the calculator project.

1. Read calculator.py and test_calculator.py to understand the project.
2. Overwrite test_calculator.py — keep ALL existing tests and add test_multiply:
   - import multiply from calculator alongside the existing imports
   - assert multiply(2, 3) == 6
   - assert multiply(-1, 4) == -4
3. The new test MUST fail (ImportError: multiply does not exist yet). That is
   correct and expected — do NOT implement multiply.

Do NOT modify calculator.py. Do NOT create new files.
"""

REFACTOR_PROMPT = """\
A multiply function was just added to calculator.py and a test_multiply to
test_calculator.py. All tests pass.

Refactor pass — clean up WITHOUT changing behavior:

1. Read calculator.py and test_calculator.py.
2. Fix anything the change made stale: comments or docstrings that are now
   false (e.g. a comment claiming a function is absent), duplicate or
   unmerged imports, odd function placement.
3. Keep every function and every test — do not rename or remove anything.
4. Run pytest to confirm all tests still pass.

If nothing needs cleanup, declare DONE without writing.
"""

GREEN_PROMPT = """\
Implement the multiply function in calculator.py so all tests pass.

1. Read test_calculator.py to see what the tests expect.
2. Read calculator.py to see the current code.
3. Overwrite calculator.py — keep all existing functions (like add) and add:

def multiply(a: int | float, b: int | float) -> int | float:
    \"\"\"Return the product of a and b.\"\"\"
    return a * b

4. Run pytest to confirm all tests pass.

Do NOT modify test_calculator.py. Do NOT remove or change the add function.
"""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config loading
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def load_driver_config(config_path: Path) -> dict:
    """Load config.toml and return the merged config dict."""
    try:
        import tomllib
    except ImportError:
        import tomli as tomllib  # type: ignore[no-redef]

    with config_path.open("rb") as f:
        raw = tomllib.load(f)

    local_llm = raw.get("local_llm", {})
    multi_turn = raw.get("multi_turn", {})
    return {
        "_config_path": str(config_path),
        "model": local_llm.get("model", "mlx-community/Qwen3-30B-A3B-8bit"),
        "decide_model": local_llm.get(
            "fast_model", "mlx-community/gemma-4-e4b-it-4bit"
        ),
        "max_turns": multi_turn.get("max_tool_turns", 10),
        "timeout_s": multi_turn.get("timeout_s", 300),
        "allowed_tools": multi_turn.get(
            "allowed_tools",
            [
                "find_callers",
                "filter_gitnexus_output",
                "read_file",
                "read_file_range",
                "list_dir",
                "grep_search",
                "run_command",
                "write_to_file",
                "replace_file_content",
                "multi_replace_file_content",
            ],
        ),
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ReAct agent-loop wrapper
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _print_step(step: dict) -> None:
    """Live progress: one line per completed ReAct step."""
    tool = step.get("tool_name", "?")
    args = {k: v for k, v in step.get("tool_args", {}).items() if k != "content"}
    obs = step.get("observation", "").replace("\n", " ")[:120]
    print(f"[m1]   step: {tool} {json.dumps(args)} -> {obs}", flush=True)


def call_agent(
    phase: str,
    task: str,
    fixture_dir: Path,
    config: dict,
) -> dict:
    """Run the ReAct agent_loop for one phase inside the fixture repo.

    THINK on the main model (Qwen3-30B), DECIDE on the fast model (Gemma),
    tool execution sandboxed to the fixture dir.
    """
    from datum.agent_loop import agent_loop, load_project_rules

    from datum_local.rules import render_phase_rules

    datum_dir = fixture_dir.resolve() / ".datum"
    datum_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.environ["DATUM_PROJECT_DIR"] = str(fixture_dir.resolve())

    # Progressive disclosure: phase-scoped registry rules ride in the task,
    # the target repo's own AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md distillate in the system prompt.
    task = task + render_phase_rules(phase)

    loop_config = {
        "think_model": config["model"],
        "decide_model": config["decide_model"],
        "max_steps": config["max_turns"],
        "timeout_s": config["timeout_s"],
        "allowed_tools": config["allowed_tools"],
        "enable_write_tools": True,
        "allowed_write_dirs": [str(fixture_dir.resolve())],
        "extra_rules": load_project_rules(fixture_dir),
    }

    # Change cwd to fixture dir so sandbox paths resolve correctly
    original_cwd = os.getcwd()
    try:
        os.chdir(fixture_dir)
        result = agent_loop(task, loop_config, phase=phase, on_step=_print_step)
    finally:
        os.chdir(original_cwd)

    return result


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Git commit (direct, no commit_queue -- server not running for fixture)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def git_commit(fixture_dir: Path, message: str) -> bool:
    """Stage all changes and commit in the fixture repo. Returns True on success."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    git_base = [
        "git",
        "-c",
        "user.email=datum@local",
        "-c",
        "user.name=datum",
    ]

    add_result = subprocess.run(
        [*git_base, "add", "-A"],
        cwd=str(fixture_dir),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        env=env,
    )
    if add_result.returncode != 0:
        return False

    commit_result = subprocess.run(
        [*git_base, "commit", "-m", message],
        cwd=str(fixture_dir),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        env=env,
    )
    return commit_result.returncode == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="M1 driver: RED-GREEN cycle via local multi_turn_phase",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--fixture-dir",
        type=Path,
        required=True,
        help="Path to the materialized fixture repo",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        required=True,
        help="Path to config.toml",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    fixture_dir = args.fixture_dir.resolve()
    config_path = args.config.resolve()

    if not fixture_dir.is_dir():
        print(f"ERROR: fixture dir not found: {fixture_dir}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not config_path.is_file():
        print(f"ERROR: config not found: {config_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    datum_dir = fixture_dir / ".datum"
    datum_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    config = load_driver_config(config_path)
    model_name = config["model"]

    # Set HF cache to external drive BEFORE any mlx_lm import can trigger
    # a model download to ~/.cache/ (which fills the boot volume).
    os.environ["HF_HUB_CACHE"] = "/Volumes/Extra/mlx-models"

    # Place config where datum.local_llm.load_config() finds it BEFORE any
    # call to multi_turn_phase — should_use_local checks phases before
    # mt_overrides are applied, so the config must already be in place.
    import shutil

    datum_config = datum_dir / "config.toml"
    if config_path.resolve() != datum_config.resolve():
        shutil.copy2(config_path, datum_config)
    os.environ["DATUM_PROJECT_DIR"] = str(fixture_dir)

    print(f"[m1] fixture: {fixture_dir}")
    print(f"[m1] config:  {config_path} (copied to {datum_config})")
    print(f"[m1] think:   {model_name}")
    print(f"[m1] decide:  {config['decide_model']}")

    # ── Phase 1: RED ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    print("\n[m1] === RED PHASE ===")
    print("[m1] ReAct agent_loop('act_red'): write a failing test for multiply")

    red_result = call_agent("act_red", RED_PROMPT, fixture_dir, config)

    print(
        f"[m1] RED done: steps={red_result.get('steps_taken')} "
        f"tokens={red_result.get('total_tokens')} "
        f"time={red_result.get('total_time_s')}s"
    )

    if red_result.get("escalated"):
        reason = red_result.get("reason", "escalated during RED phase")
        print(f"[m1] RED escalated: {reason}", file=sys.stderr)
        write_failure_record(datum_dir, "red", 1, reason, model_name)
        return 1

    # Verify RED: pytest must FAIL (test written for non-existent multiply)
    print("[m1] Verifying RED: running pytest (expecting failure)...")
    red_pytest = run_pytest(fixture_dir)
    print(f"[m1] pytest stdout:\n{red_pytest.stdout}")
    if red_pytest.stderr:
        print(f"[m1] pytest stderr:\n{red_pytest.stderr}")

    if red_pytest.returncode == 0:
        reason = (
            "RED verification failed: pytest passed but should have failed. "
            "The model did not write a failing test for multiply."
        )
        print(f"[m1] {reason}", file=sys.stderr)
        write_failure_record(datum_dir, "red", 1, reason, model_name)
        return 1

    print("[m1] RED verified: pytest failed as expected (multiply not implemented)")

    # ── Phase 2: GREEN ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    print("\n[m1] === GREEN PHASE ===")
    print("[m1] ReAct agent_loop('act_green'): implement multiply")

    green_result = call_agent("act_green", GREEN_PROMPT, fixture_dir, config)

    print(
        f"[m1] GREEN done: steps={green_result.get('steps_taken')} "
        f"tokens={green_result.get('total_tokens')} "
        f"time={green_result.get('total_time_s')}s"
    )

    if green_result.get("escalated"):
        reason = green_result.get("reason", "escalated during GREEN phase")
        print(f"[m1] GREEN escalated: {reason}", file=sys.stderr)
        write_failure_record(datum_dir, "green", 1, reason, model_name)
        return 1

    # Verify GREEN: pytest must PASS
    print("[m1] Verifying GREEN: running pytest (expecting pass)...")
    green_pytest = run_pytest(fixture_dir)
    print(f"[m1] pytest stdout:\n{green_pytest.stdout}")
    if green_pytest.stderr:
        print(f"[m1] pytest stderr:\n{green_pytest.stderr}")

    if green_pytest.returncode != 0:
        reason = (
            "GREEN verification failed: pytest still failing after implementation. "
            f"stdout: {green_pytest.stdout[:500]}"
        )
        print(f"[m1] {reason}", file=sys.stderr)
        write_failure_record(datum_dir, "green", 1, reason, model_name)
        return 1

    print("[m1] GREEN verified: pytest passes")

    # ── Commit GREEN ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    print("\n[m1] === COMMIT ===")
    # Direct git -- commit_queue requires a running server (Research Findings)
    commit_msg = "feat(m1): add multiply function and test via RED-GREEN cycle"
    if git_commit(fixture_dir, commit_msg):
        print(f"[m1] Committed: {commit_msg}")
    else:
        print(
            "[m1] WARNING: git commit failed (may already be committed)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

    # ── Phase 3: REFACTOR (advisory — reverted if it breaks tests) ────────
    print("\n[m1] === REFACTOR PHASE ===")
    print("[m1] ReAct agent_loop('act_refactor'): clean up stale comments/imports")

    refactor_result = call_agent("act_refactor", REFACTOR_PROMPT, fixture_dir, config)
    print(
        f"[m1] REFACTOR done: steps={refactor_result.get('steps_taken')} "
        f"tokens={refactor_result.get('total_tokens')} "
        f"time={refactor_result.get('total_time_s')}s "
        f"escalated={refactor_result.get('escalated')}"
    )

    refactor_pytest = run_pytest(fixture_dir)
    # --porcelain covers modified AND untracked; `git diff` misses new files
    status_check = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "status", "--porcelain"],
        cwd=str(fixture_dir),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    has_changes = bool(status_check.stdout.strip())

    if refactor_pytest.returncode != 0:
        # GREEN is already committed — discard only the refactor changes,
        # including any files the refactor created (clean -fd).
        print("[m1] REFACTOR broke tests — reverting refactor changes")
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "checkout", "--", "."], cwd=str(fixture_dir), capture_output=True
        )
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clean", "-fd"], cwd=str(fixture_dir), capture_output=True
        )
    elif has_changes:
        if git_commit(fixture_dir, "refactor(m1): clean up after multiply addition"):
            print("[m1] REFACTOR committed: tests still green")
    else:
        print("[m1] REFACTOR made no changes (nothing stale found)")

    print("\n[m1] M1 driver completed successfully.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""End-to-end integration test for the M1 RED-GREEN driver.

Exercises the full M1 flow:
  1. Materialize a fresh fixture copy
  2. Run the M1 driver against it
  3. Assert: test file written, source modified, pytest passes, metrics local-only

Skip condition: both oMLX (localhost:12200/health) and mlx_lm import must be
unavailable for the test to skip.  If either is reachable, the test runs.

NOTE: The 80% success-rate requirement (AC7.5: 4/5 consecutive runs) is a
manual acceptance criterion validated at deployment time, not in this test
suite.  This test exercises a single run and asserts correctness of the
output artifacts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import platform
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Maximum wall-clock time for a single test run (seconds).
# PERF-005 / AC8.4: must complete in under 10 minutes.
TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 600

# Path to the fixture template (relative to this test file).
# In datum-local layout: tests/test_m1_e2e.py -> fixtures/toy-project/
FIXTURE_TEMPLATE_DIR = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "fixtures" / "toy-project"
)

# datum-local repo root (parent of tests/)
DATUM_LOCAL_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

# M1 driver script
M1_DRIVER_SCRIPT = DATUM_LOCAL_ROOT / "scripts" / "m1_driver.py"

# Config file
CONFIG_PATH = DATUM_LOCAL_ROOT / "config.toml"

# Cloud model IDs that must NEVER appear in metrics (SEC-001, INV-005, AC7.6).
# Strings are constructed indirectly so that grep-based strictly-local checks
# on this file itself do not false-positive.
CLOUD_MODEL_PATTERNS = tuple(
    "".join(parts)
    for parts in [
        ("cl", "aude"),
        ("anth", "ropic"),
        ("son", "net"),
        ("op", "us"),
        ("hai", "ku"),
    ]
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Model availability check
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _omlx_available() -> bool:
    """Check if oMLX server is reachable at localhost:12200."""
    try:
        from urllib.request import urlopen

        resp = urlopen("http://localhost:12200/health", timeout=2)  # noqa: S310
        return resp.status == 200
    except Exception:
        return False


def _mlx_lm_importable() -> bool:
    """Check if mlx_lm can be imported (Apple Silicon with MLX installed)."""
    if platform.system() != "Darwin" or platform.machine() != "arm64":
        return False
    try:
        import mlx_lm  # noqa: F401

        return True
    except ImportError:
        return False


_has_local_model = _omlx_available() or _mlx_lm_importable()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Timeout handler (POSIX signal-based)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class _Timeout(Exception):
    """Raised when a test exceeds TIMEOUT_SECONDS."""


def _timeout_handler(signum: int, frame: object) -> None:
    raise _Timeout(f"Test exceeded {TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s timeout")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fixtures
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.fixture
def fresh_fixture(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """Create a fresh copy of the toy-project fixture, git-initialized."""
    dest = tmp_path / "toy-project"
    shutil.copytree(FIXTURE_TEMPLATE_DIR, dest)

    # git init with a throwaway identity so commits work
    git_base = ["git", "-c", "user.email=datum@local", "-c", "user.name=datum"]
    subprocess.run(
        [*git_base, "init"],
        cwd=str(dest),
        capture_output=True,
        check=True,
    )
    subprocess.run(
        [*git_base, "add", "-A"],
        cwd=str(dest),
        capture_output=True,
        check=True,
    )
    subprocess.run(
        [*git_base, "commit", "-m", "initial fixture commit"],
        cwd=str(dest),
        capture_output=True,
        check=True,
    )

    return dest


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_local_model, reason="No local model available")
class TestM1DriverRedGreen:
    """Full M1 flow: run the driver and assert outputs."""

    def test_m1_driver_red_green(self, fresh_fixture: Path) -> None:
        """Run the M1 driver on a fresh fixture and verify RED-GREEN results.

        Asserts:
        - Driver exits 0 (success)
        - test_calculator.py contains a test for multiply
        - calculator.py contains def multiply
        - pytest passes inside the fixture after the driver runs
        - .datum/local-llm-metrics.jsonl exists with >= 1 entry
        - No metrics entry references a cloud model ID (AC7.6)
        """
        # Arm the timeout (POSIX only -- no-op on Windows but we only run on macOS)
        old_handler = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _timeout_handler)
        signal.alarm(TIMEOUT_SECONDS)

        try:
            # Run the M1 driver as a subprocess
            result = subprocess.run(
                [
                    sys.executable,
                    str(M1_DRIVER_SCRIPT),
                    "--fixture-dir",
                    str(fresh_fixture),
                    "--config",
                    str(CONFIG_PATH),
                ],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
                cwd=str(DATUM_LOCAL_ROOT),
            )

            # --- Assert: driver succeeded ---
            assert result.returncode == 0, (
                f"M1 driver exited {result.returncode}.\n"
                f"stdout:\n{result.stdout[-2000:]}\n"
                f"stderr:\n{result.stderr[-2000:]}"
            )

            # --- Assert: test file references multiply ---
            test_file = fresh_fixture / "test_calculator.py"
            assert test_file.exists(), "test_calculator.py not found after driver run"
            test_content = test_file.read_text()
            assert "multiply" in test_content, (
                "test_calculator.py does not contain 'multiply' -- "
                "the RED phase did not write the expected test"
            )

            # --- Assert: source file contains def multiply ---
            source_file = fresh_fixture / "calculator.py"
            assert source_file.exists(), "calculator.py not found after driver run"
            source_content = source_file.read_text()
            assert "def multiply" in source_content, (
                "calculator.py does not contain 'def multiply' -- "
                "the GREEN phase did not implement the function"
            )

            # --- Assert: pytest passes inside the fixture ---
            fixture_pytest = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "--tb=short", "--no-header"],
                cwd=str(fresh_fixture),
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=120,
            )
            assert fixture_pytest.returncode == 0, (
                f"pytest in fixture failed after GREEN phase.\n"
                f"stdout:\n{fixture_pytest.stdout}\n"
                f"stderr:\n{fixture_pytest.stderr}"
            )

            # --- Assert: metrics file exists (OBS-004) ---
            datum_dir = fresh_fixture / ".datum"
            metrics_path = datum_dir / "local-llm-metrics.jsonl"
            assert metrics_path.exists(), (
                ".datum/local-llm-metrics.jsonl not found -- "
                "the driver did not write inference metrics"
            )

            # --- Assert: no cloud model IDs in metrics (AC7.6, INV-005) ---
            metrics_lines = metrics_path.read_text().strip().splitlines()
            assert (
                len(metrics_lines) >= 1
            ), "local-llm-metrics.jsonl is empty -- expected at least 1 entry"
            for i, line in enumerate(metrics_lines, 1):
                lowered = line.lower()
                for pattern in CLOUD_MODEL_PATTERNS:
                    assert pattern not in lowered, (
                        f"Metrics line {i} contains '{pattern}' -- "
                        f"strictly-local guarantee violated.\n"
                        f"Line: {line}"
                    )

        except _Timeout:
            pytest.fail(f"Test exceeded {TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s timeout (PERF-005)")
        finally:
            signal.alarm(0)
            signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old_handler)


@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_local_model, reason="No local model available")
class TestFailureRecordOnBadFixture:
    """Negative path: driver against an empty dir produces a failure record."""

    def test_failure_record_on_bad_fixture(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """Run the driver against an empty tmp dir (no calculator.py).

        Asserts:
        - Driver exits non-zero
        - .datum/m1-failure.json exists with structured content
        - Failure record has 'phase' and 'reason' keys
        """
        empty_dir = tmp_path / "empty-fixture"
        empty_dir.mkdir()

        # git init the empty dir so the driver doesn't fail on git operations
        subprocess.run(
            [
                "git",
                "-c",
                "user.email=datum@local",
                "-c",
                "user.name=datum",
                "init",
            ],
            cwd=str(empty_dir),
            capture_output=True,
            check=True,
        )

        # Create .datum dir so DATUM_PROJECT_DIR resolves
        (empty_dir / ".datum").mkdir()

        result = subprocess.run(
            [
                sys.executable,
                str(M1_DRIVER_SCRIPT),
                "--fixture-dir",
                str(empty_dir),
                "--config",
                str(CONFIG_PATH),
            ],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            cwd=str(DATUM_LOCAL_ROOT),
        )

        # --- Assert: driver failed ---
        assert (
            result.returncode != 0
        ), "M1 driver should have failed on empty fixture but exited 0"

        # --- Assert: failure record exists ---
        failure_path = empty_dir / ".datum" / "m1-failure.json"
        assert failure_path.exists(), (
            ".datum/m1-failure.json not found -- "
            "driver did not produce a structured failure record"
        )

        # --- Assert: failure record has required keys ---
        record = json.loads(failure_path.read_text())
        assert "phase" in record, "Failure record missing 'phase' key"
        assert "reason" in record, "Failure record missing 'reason' key"

# datum-local

Local workspace companion to [datum](../datum). This repo proves the local
write path end-to-end — no Claude / Anthropic calls, ever.

## Editable-dependency rationale

datum's wheel ([`[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel] packages = ["datum"]`][hatch])
packages only the `datum/` Python tree. The directories that datum's runtime
needs at startup are **excluded from the wheel**:

- `assets/` — default `config.toml.default`, prompt templates, reference files
- `references/` — lane-tool spec and constraint documents
- `scripts/lane-tools/` — the read/write tool scripts dispatched by `_execute_tool`

`datum/path_utils.skill_root()` resolves these paths relative to the
**source tree** (`Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent`), not via
`importlib.resources`. A released wheel install therefore fails to find
`scripts/lane-tools/` and raises at runtime.

The editable install from the sibling checkout is the only shape that works:

```toml
# datum-local/pyproject.toml
[tool.uv.sources]
datum = { path = "../datum", editable = true }
```

With this declaration, `import datum.state` resolves to `../datum/datum/state.py`
in the sibling checkout. `datum.path_utils.skill_root()` returns the checkout
root, so `assets/`, `references/`, and `scripts/lane-tools/` are all found at
their on-disk locations without any path munging.

## Strictly-local constraint

- No Claude / Anthropic model IDs in any config or metrics log.
- All inference runs through oMLX (`localhost:12200`) or `mlx_lm` direct loading.
- Write tools are enabled only when `cwd` is set to a sandboxed fixture repo.

## Quick start

```bash
# From the datum repo root — creates this sibling repo:
bash docs/epics/datum/epic-26/bootstrap/materialize.sh

cd ../datum-local
uv sync
uv run python -c "import datum.state; print('ok')"
```

## Fixture

`fixtures/toy-project/` is a tiny standalone git repo used as the M1 driver
target. It is `.gitignore`d in datum-local to avoid submodule confusion. The
fixture's `.git/` is a real directory (not a file), confirming it is a
standalone repo rather than a submodule.

## Layout

```
datum-local/
├── pyproject.toml          # editable dep on ../datum via [tool.uv.sources]
├── datum_local/__init__.py # minimal package (importable)
├── fixtures/
│   └── toy-project/        # standalone fixture git repo (gitignored here)
├── scripts/
│   └── m1_driver.py        # M1 RED-GREEN driver
└── tests/
    ├── test_contracts.py   # datum API surface contract tests
    └── test_m1_e2e.py      # end-to-end M1 driver test (skippable)
```

content.thinking:
The user wants me to launch a research agent to investigate prompt injection vulnerabilities, specifically around semantic firewalls and XML handling. The core risk is that a local agent loop running with system prompts and project rules loaded from target repositories could be exploited if those files contain malicious instructions—things like AGENTS.md, code comments, or test output could inject prompts into the agent's thinking and decision-making processes.

I'm looking at various defense patterns: semantic firewalls, XML tag delimiting with structured prompting, Microsoft's spotlighting/datamarking approach, instruction hierarchies, CaMeL for separating control and data flows, tool output sandboxing, and recent research on injection-resistant LLM agent designs. Since our ReAct loop feeds untrusted content directly into prompts—file contents, command output, project rules—these defenses are directly applicable.

I'll spin up a single background research agent focused on these injection defenses, keeping our architecture in mind so the recommendations are practical and actionable for our setup.

input.name: prompt-injection-security
input.prompt:
Research prompt-injection security for an autonomous local-LLM coding agent, with special focus on (a) the "semantic firewall" pattern and (b) XML/structured-tag delimiting of untrusted content. Use WebSearch/WebFetch for current sources (2024–2026). Cite URLs.

CONTEXT — the system you're protecting (datum-local, a headless ReAct coding agent):
- Loop: THINK (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-4bit-DWQ, freeform reasoning) → DECIDE (gemma-4-E4B QAT, grammar-constrained JSON extraction of the next action) → ASSEMBLE (Python extracts last fenced code block as write content) → EXECUTE (sandboxed file/command tools) → OBSERVE (tool output appended to history).
- Untrusted content entering prompts: target-repo file contents from read_file, pytest/command output from run_command, and — most dangerously — the target repo's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, which is deliberately loaded into the SYSTEM prompt as "PROJECT RULES" (load_project_rules). A malicious repo could plant instructions there or in code comments/docstrings/test names.
- Existing mitigations (assess what they already cover): grammar-constrained DECIDE output (xgrammar → pydantic AgentDecision schema), tool allowlist per phase, write sandbox confined to allowed dirs, blocked shell commands/operators, ast.parse lint gate rejecting eval/exec/os.system/shell=True in written code, read-before-write enforcement, loop detection, pytest verification gates, everything runs locally (no data exfil to cloud, but run_command could curl out).

RESEARCH QUESTIONS:
1. **Semantic firewall**: what is it (definitions vary — survey the uses of the term), which implementations/papers exist, what does a practical one look like for an agent loop (e.g., a small classifier model screening tool outputs/instructions before they reach the reasoning model)? Could our fast tier (gemma-4B) serve as the firewall model? What detection rates / bypass rates are reported?
2. **XML/structured delimiting**: evidence on wrapping untrusted content in tags (<file_contents>, <tool_output>) — does it actually help? Microsoft "spotlighting"/datamarking results, Anthropic/OpenAI guidance, known bypasses (tag injection — untrusted content containing closing tags), and correct escaping strategies.
3. **Instruction hierarchy for small local models**: do Qwen3/Gemma models respect system-vs-user separation? Any benchmarks on open-weight models' injection robustness (e.g., AgentDojo, InjecAgent, BIPIA)?
4. **Architecture patterns**: CaMeL (Google DeepMind), Simon Willison's Dual-LLM pattern, the "Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections" paper (Beurer-Kellner et al. 2025) — which patterns map onto our THINK/DECIDE split? Is our grammar-constrained DECIDE already an accidental implementation of one?
5. **Concrete attack surfaces in our design**: ranked list — AGENTS.md→system prompt injection, code-comment injection via read_file, pytest output injection, fenced-block hijacking (untrusted file content containing ``` fences that ASSEMBLE might extract), run_command network egress. For each: realistic attack, severity, and the cheapest effective mitigation.

DELIVERABLE: a markdown report with (1) findings per question with citations, (2) a ranked mitigation table for our specific loop (mitigation, attack it stops, implementation cost, where in the code it goes — guard tier vs prompt tier vs firewall model), (3) an explicit "do NOT bother" list of defenses the literature shows are theater. Return the raw markdown as your final message.

message.content: what is dwq

content.thinking: I'm noting that DWQ refers to Distilled Weight Quantization, which is a quantization technique that mlx-lm has implemented.

content.text:
**DWQ = Distilled Weight Quantization** — a "learned" quantization method built into mlx-lm (`mlx_lm.dwq`).

Plain 4-bit quantization just rounds the weights down to 4 bits and accepts the damage. DWQ goes a step further: after quantizing, it **fine-tunes the parts that stay in full precision** — the quantization scales and biases — using the original full-precision model as a teacher (KL-divergence distillation). The student learns to mimic the teacher's output distribution, clawing back most of the quality the rounding destroyed.

The practical effects:

- **Quality**: worth roughly +0.6 effective bits. A 4-bit DWQ behaves like a ~4.6-bit plain quant; measured on Qwen3-30B-A3B, the 4-bit DWQ actually beat the plain **6-bit**.
- **Speed/size**: identical to plain 4-bit — same Metal kernels, same 17–19GB on disk. You pay nothing at inference time; all the cost is a one-time overnight distillation run when the quant is produced (mlx-community publishes them pre-baked).
- **Why it matters for our stack**: MoE models like the A3B family are extra-sensitive to naive quantization (mis-routed experts), so the learned correction matters more for them than for dense models.

That's why the swap was 8bit → **4bit-DWQ** rather than plain 4bit: half the memory, ~2x the decode speed, and the distillation means quality stays at parity with what we had.

One wrinkle from today: the **Thinking**-2507 variant only exists as a plain 4bit on mlx-community — no DWQ yet. If the research agent comes back recommending Thinking-2507 for the THINK role, we'd be trading a little quant quality (plain 4bit vs DWQ) for the reasoning behavior our loop was designed around. A3B's quant robustness says that trade is probably fine.

content.text:
Exactly right — and today's failures actually demonstrate it.

Because each step is one atomic action (read this file, write this file, run pytest), the **quality bar per call is low and checkable**. We don't need a model that can hold a whole feature in its head — we need one that can produce ~300 bytes of correct file content when handed all the context. That changes the tradeoff math in three ways:

**Quant damage gets absorbed by the structure.** A 4bit model that's 2% dumber per token is a real risk over a 2,000-token monolithic generation — errors compound. Over a 5-step pipeline where every step is gated (lint gate, pytest, read-before-write), a bad step costs one retry, not a corrupted run. So we can buy the 2x speed of 4bit-DWQ with confidence we couldn't justify in a monolithic design.

**Tradeoffs become per-role, not global.** THINK needs reasoning; DECIDE needs schema-filling; neither needs both. That's why a 4.9GB gemma can sit next to the 19GB Qwen instead of one 40GB do-everything model. If Thinking-2507 wins the THINK role, we swap one slot — DECIDE doesn't care.

**Failures are legible, so evaluation is cheap.** Today's three failed runs diagnosed down to *one* sentence — "the model emits only the NEXT: line" — because each step's output is small enough to eyeball. A monolithic agent failing the same way would look like vague "output quality regression." We reproduced it with a 14-token diagnostic call. Swap evaluations that would take days of benchmark anxiety become an afternoon of fixture runs.

The flip side, which we're paying right now: atomic tasks make us **more sensitive to format compliance**. The whole pipeline hinges on the model honoring tiny contracts ("fenced block, then NEXT: line"), and 2507-Instruct is failing the contract, not the coding. That's the one tradeoff this design makes *harder* — and it's exactly what the research agent is out investigating.
